reason: This book was already repositioned defensively (39% cash, the MSTR short added specifically to fade a cracking Bitcoin blow-off top) and the last 48-72 hours of tape has validated rather than undermined that call, so I see no informational edge to trading ahead of tomorrow's FOMC print. Rate pricing (CME FedWatch-style) shows roughly 90% odds of a hold at 3.75-4.00% versus ~10% for a 25bp cut on 2026-09-16 -- essentially the outcome the book was already built around when cash was raised for a 'newly hawkish rate regime,' so there's no new macro surprise to react to yet. The MSTR short is working (+2.45% on the leg, stock down to $130.80, -4.48% on the day) even as some sell-side desks raise price targets on Bitcoin-correlation optimism -- that divergence is exactly the fade this leg is meant to capture, and the 15% stop already caps the risk if BTC reasserts itself. JPM and CVX are flat-to-green with no negative catalyst (JPM's exposure to the Situational Awareness AI-lending blowup is a headline risk to monitor, not yet a thesis-breaker for a mega-bank). XBI's -3.82% leg reads as normal consolidation after testing 52-week highs near $170, not a breakdown -- biotech M&A remains robust ($106B across 201 deals YTD) and healthcare is being framed as a rotation destination out of stretched tech, which supports rather than undercuts the position. ELV is already up +4.88% and was deliberately sized down as a profit-take, consistent with the current strategy. Given the high cash buffer already absorbs event risk and a full replacement would burn real bps and risk breaching the Round 3 novelty rule against my own Round 2 book for no clear gain, the better decision is to hold through the FOMC print and reassess with the actual outcome in hand.
